description:
Follow-up to fz-qe0, which removed the dominant term (the recursive-group reachability walk stepping into settled products: 21.9M node visits -> 9.9K, run 12.2s -> 3.9s).

The fixture is still ~2.6s interp / ~3.1s run, which by the standing convention (tiny fixtures must finish in ms-to-tenths; >1s is a correctness signal, not a perf one) is still excess work.

MEASURED at fz-qe0 HEAD, --log-telemetry, interp lane, time attributed to the gap preceding each product settle:
  executable_facts          533 settles    429 ms
  runtime_demand              3 settles    343 ms
  callable_construction    2625 settles    229 ms   (was 6704 ms)
  transport_shape          2702 settles    159 ms
  abi_executable            242 settles     65 ms
plus ~0.9s inside drive jobs, of which AnalyzeActivation is 921 spans / 791 ms.

THE SIGNAL IS THE COUNT, NOT THE COST. There are 242 executables but 2625 callable_construction and 2702 transport_shape settlements -- about 11 of each per executable. Each is now cheap, so the wall clock no longer screams, but the population is the thing to explain: either those are genuinely distinct positions, or products are re-settling (churn). Establish which BEFORE optimizing anything -- if it is churn it belongs to the fz-go4.18.28 transport-monolith / partial-publication family and the fix is upstream.

Likewise 921 AnalyzeActivation spans for this fixture is worth a census against the activation inventory.

FIRST STEP: count DISTINCT ProductKeys settled per kind versus total settlements. Equal => genuine population, look at why the position count is 11x the executable count. Unequal => churn, and the re-settle triggers are the lead.

DO NOT fix by raising the fixture budget. fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz now pins run/interp at 6s specifically so this stays visible.
title: enum_predicate_search still compiles for ~3s after the settled-product pruning: 2625 callable_construction settlements for 242 executables
